text:
anna-ng: quick sync — i've been prototyping an "edge allocator" shim that enforces region affinity + soft-sla bins before hitting the routing policy engine. looking for feedback on tradeoffs.

mike-t: curious — is this to reduce cross-region latency or to limit inter-region egress costs?

anna-ng: both. main goals: 1) prefer local region when p95 latency > target, 2) avoid expensive egress unless absolutely necessary, 3) expose a cheap fallback path for degraded capacity.

julia-chen: do you mean a pre-filter before the policy engine? how do we ensure it doesn't fight existing routing rules?

anna-ng: yes pre-filter. idea is a small deterministic stage: compute a candidate pool using region/capacity/tier heuristics, then hand off to policy engine which applies cost/latency/tier scoring. the pre-filter reduces cardinality and protects the engine from flapping when a region is intermittently degraded.

kevin-p: i worry about correctness — if pre-filter drops a region that the policy would have chosen (because of cost), we might change observable decisions. any plan for consistency/telemetry?

anna-ng: good call. plan: emit metrics for pre-filter rejections and keep an "opt-out" flag per-tenant so we can run an A/B. also keep a debug header that forces full evaluation.

sre-luke: what about SLA tiers? enterprise customers might pin region or demand hard latency SLOs. pre-filter needs to respect hard constraints first.

anna-ng: agreed — pre-filter rules will be applied in order: 1) hard constraints (pin/mandatory region, hard SLA), 2) soft affinity (prefer local region, but allow fallback), 3) capacity cutoffs. fallback policy still allowed to route to other regions if no candidates.

mike-t: can we express the pre-filter in the policy DSL so it's auditable? i want to avoid a magic blackbox.

anna-ng: i prototyped a compact JSON expression that maps neatly to our DSL. idea: small declarative block that the router compiles to a fast evaluator. example attached: 
```json
{
  "pre_filter": {
    "order": ["hard", "soft_affinity", "capacity"],
    "hard": {"region_pin": "request.metadata.region"},
    "soft_affinity": {"prefer_region": "request.metadata.region", "penalty": 0.2},
    "capacity": {"min_free_slots": 10, "min_gpu_mem_mb": 12000}
  }
}
```

julia-chen: that looks reasonable. two thoughts: 1) penalty semantics need to be well-defined vs other cost components, 2) min_free_slots is brittle across model families.

kevin-p: on (2) — maybe express capacity as a percentile over recent windows (e.g., free_slots_p50 > 10) so it adapts.

anna-ng: yep, will swap to time-windowed heuristics. also thinking about a tiny local cache of recent routing decisions to improve stability — like stickiness for 5s per-client. avoids flipping for retry storms.

sre-luke: sounds helpful for reducing cascading failures. does the cache interact badly with canary rollouts?

anna-ng: we can tie stickiness to rollout flags; by default respects canary weight. if a tenant is in canary, stickiness is scoped per variant so you won't pin to the wrong cluster.

mike-t: what's the fallback strategy when pre-filter yields empty candidate set? do we return 503 or broaden rules?

anna-ng: broadening. order: (a) relax soft affinity penalties, (b) relax capacity thresholds (with higher cost weight), (c) allow cross-region but mark "egress_cost" tag. only 503 if none of those succeed.

kevin-p: need to be careful with billing signals — if we mark egregious egress as higher cost, the optimizer might still pick it for short requests. we should put a hard cap per minute to prevent runaway egress.

anna-ng: agreed — add a circuit-breaker: per-tenant egress_budget_tokens per window. once budget exhausted, deny cross-region until budget refilled.

julia-chen: how do we validate quality after fallback? model variants across regions might differ (quantization/version). idea: couple fallback with a quick eval sample to check hallucination/latency before returning.

anna-ng: interesting — lightweight health probes on the path. we could do async sampling for long-lived tenants and immediate synthetic probe for first few fallbacks. cost-y but helps prevent quality regressions.

sre-luke: ops-bot: can we add a monitor for cross-region fallbacks > 1% of requests? want alerts before SLA impacts.

ops-bot: noted — creating monitor 'routing.cross_region_fallback_rate' with 1% threshold for production.

mike-t: is there any compatibility issue with dedicated/private deployments? private installs might not allow cross-region so pre-filter must be configurable per-deployment.

anna-ng: yes, config toggle per-deployment. default behavior varies: hosted = allow cross-region with egress controls; private = no-cross-region unless customer explicitly enables peering.

kevin-p: operationally, who owns the pre-filter component? infra or routing team?

anna-ng: runtime infra will own the shim, routing team owns the DSL and scoring interface. infra implements the fast evaluator and metrics hooks.

julia-chen: can we add a short RFC enumerating: API surface, DSL snippet, metrics, circuit-breaker behavior, and rollout plan? i'll volunteer to do the metrics/observability section.

anna-ng: thanks — i'll draft the RFC. proposed rollout: internal canary (10% traffic) in staging for 48h, then 5% in prod (opt-in tenants), ramp to 50% after 7 days of stable metrics.

mike-t: +1 to the plan. one last ask: include a small simulation with historical traffic to show how frequently pre-filter would have changed decisions.

anna-ng: will run sims and add to RFC.

kevin-p: LGTM. add me as reviewer.

julia-chen: same.

anna-ng: great — i'll post RFC link when ready. thx all :shipit:
